public_rationale: The first part holds. GPT-4's own technical report says it is a model pre-trained to predict the next token in a document (e1). So its output does come from a statistical process of predicting likely words, refined by post-training. The 'NEVER fact-check' part does not hold as a universal claim. In September 2023, Google's Bard gained a feature that reads its own answer and checks it against web content (e2). Also in September 2023, Meta researchers showed an LLM planning and answering questions to fact-check its own draft (e3). Both came well before the April 2024 post. By default, a bare model does not check its claims, which is likely what Marcus meant.
limitations: Bard's check relies on Google Search, a tool outside the model; a reader who limits 'LLMs' to the bare model may discount it.
Chain-of-Verification needs a special prompt and is not default behavior.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: All LLM output, true or false, comes from the same statistical word-reconstruction process, and LLMs never fact-check what they say.

statement.excerpt: Instead, everything that LLMs say -- true or false -- comes from the same process of statistically reconstructing what words are likely in some context. They NEVER fact-check what they say.
statement.document_title: Humans versus Machines: The Hallucination Edition

from_speaker: everything that LLMs say -- true or false
comes from the same process of statistically reconstructing what words are likely in some context
They NEVER fact-check what they say
our_interpretation: Plain reading: LLM outputs are produced by next-token prediction, and LLMs never check their claims.
He names no period. The claim describes the state of LLMs when the post appeared. The target period runs from GPT-4's release (March 2023) to the post date (2024-04-21).
'NEVER' is a universal claim. One documented case of an LLM, or an LLM product, checking its own claims counts against it.
criteria.support_condition: Documentation shows LLMs generate text by next-token prediction and no LLM checked its own claims during the period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented LLM method or deployed LLM feature from the period checks the model's own claims.

evidence.excerpt: GPT-4 is a Transformer-based model pre-trained to predict the next token in a document.
evidence.explanation: This supports the first part. The leading LLM generates text by predicting likely next tokens. The report also notes post-training, which shapes but does not replace that process.

evidence.excerpt: When you click on the “G” icon, Bard will read the response and evaluate whether there is content across the web to substantiate it.
evidence.locator: Section 'Easily double-check responses and build on shared conversations'
evidence.explanation: From September 2023, Google's deployed LLM product, at the user's request, checked its own answers against web content. This contradicts 'NEVER fact-check' as applied to LLM products.
